transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Marcus Holt (Redwood); Alex Rui, Mei Chen, Carlos Ortega, Samir Patel, Lydia (NovoMetrics)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to confirm capacity uplift and add EU region + burst capacity window. Discussed hosted vs dedicated for sensitive workloads, SSO/KMS, audit logs and contract amendment timing. Agreed to run a short benchmark.

Topics: contract extension length, reserved capacity vs burst, EU data residency, performance SLAs, procurement timeline.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
00:00 Jordan Lee: all right everyone good afternoon, this is Jordan from Redwood here with Priya and Marcus, thanks for joining. can you hear me okay?
00:07 Alex Rui: yep loud and clear, thanks. we're on a slightly tighter agenda today, figured we'd keep it focused.
00:12 Priya Nair: cool, we'll run through current usage, proposed uplift, and then go into the EU region questions and security.
00:20 Mei Chen: quick note — we're coming up on our fiscal renewal window end of september so timeline is tight.
00:26 Jordan Lee: understood, thanks Mei. duration wise we have 42 minutes, we want to leave time for procurement questions.
00:33 Carlos Ortega: yep procurement is mostly price + contract amendments, also need SDSA and SOC docs, that's standard.
00:40 Marcus Holt: we have the SOC 2 bundle and ISO stub, i'll share links after the call.
00:45 Lydia: i'm from security, a couple quick asks: KMS integration, audit log retention to two years, and confirmation on isolation for EU workloads.
00:55 Priya Nair: noted, KMS— we support Bring Your Own Key via standard KMS flows and HSM on dedicated/private. audit logs are available through the console with longer retention via add-on.
01:05 Alex Rui: for the EU thing — we need EU-only processing for PII streams, everything else can remain in us-east. curious what config would look like.
01:15 Priya Nair: two options: 1) Redwood Hosted with routing rules to EU region and data residency controls; 2) Redwood Private (on VPC) dedicated for EU-only sensitive workloads. tradeoff is cost vs operational control.
01:28 Mei Chen: What about latency for EU users if we keep model serving in the US? some of our interactive features need <120ms tail latency.
01:37 Priya Nair: if you need sub-120ms tail we recommend dedicated capacity in the EU region; hosted can hit 200-300ms for the model sizes you're using. but with caching and prefix KV the p95 for some workloads improves.
01:50 Samir Patel: just to add: our gen prompts are long — average seq 1.2k — KV cache helps but token cost becomes material. curious about quantization profiles you recommend.
02:03 Priya Nair: yes for long context we suggest int4 quantized variants for batch throughput; Redwood Optimize has suggestions but for interactive single-request latency int8 might strike the best perf/cost balance.
02:17 Alex Rui: reminder — our legal needs a clause for fallback routing — if EU capacity is saturated can traffic fall back to other regions? that's a compliance question.
02:26 Jordan Lee: we can set automated routing policies with on/off fallbacks; for strict EU-only processing the Private option is safer since fallback's disabled. otherwise we can do geo-fencing with no-fallback for specific endpoints.
02:41 Lydia: important — no-fallback is required for EU-PII endpoints.
02:45 Priya Nair: understood. we'll mark those as non-fallthrough routes.
02:49 Carlos Ortega: on pricing — we're looking at a 30% uplift in committed capacity for the next 12 months plus a small burst pool for holiday spikes. what does that look like?
03:00 Jordan Lee: great question. high-level options: reserved capacity monthly commit (discounted) + burst credits billed on use; or a tiered buffer that triggers autoscale. We proposed a 30% uplift sheet earlier, today we want to firm numbers.
03:14 Mei Chen: can you show an example cost for our baseline (current usage) + 30% uplift vs dedicated EU pool?
03:20 Jordan Lee: yes, priya will share a dedicated sizing spreadsheet. quick numbers: hosted uplift would be roughly 1.18x current spend for the uplift plus burst at list rates; dedicated EU pool upfront commit gives ~25-35% lower per-token cost but with commitment.
03:35 Samir Patel: we also run offline batch embeddings — any guidance on separating batch from online to save cost?
03:41 Priya Nair: separate queues; batch can run on cheaper reserved nodes with different quantization, embeddings are cheaper as a different SKU. Redwood Console supports per-route budgets.
03:51 Alex Rui: competitors like AtlasAI quoted us a lower per-token but didn't include enterprise SLA or audit logs. tradeoff is real.
03:59 Jordan Lee: Understood. Our pitch is predictable economics + observability.
04:03 Mei Chen: procurement question — for an amendment vs new contract, what clauses change for reserved capacity?
04:09 Marcus Holt: typical amendment adds a schedule with reserved capacity amounts, revised termination, and service level appendix. we'll provide a sample amendment PDF.
04:18 Carlos Ortega: timeline wise we need internal approvals by 2027-08-25 to sign before september. can you get pricing to us by Thursday?
04:25 Jordan Lee: yes aim is to have updated pricing + burst worksheet by 2027-08-18. that's action item for me.
04:30 Lydia: security — curious about e2e encryption in transit and at rest. also whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys for logs.
04:38 Priya Nair: TLS in transit, at-rest encryption with KMS. we support CMK for model artifacts and optionally for logs with Private. We'll document exact key paths.
04:52 Samir Patel: quick technical — are you able to reserve GPUs for our peak batch window (overnight) separate from interactive pool?
04:59 Priya Nair: yes that's a common pattern: separate pool + autoscale windowing. We'll propose a nightly reservation cadence.
05:07 Alex Rui: can we run a 1-hour benchmark next week to verify tail latencies for our top-10 prompts against proposed dedicated sizing?
05:15 Priya Nair: absolutely. Samir, can you share the prompt set and we'll coordinate times?
05:20 Samir Patel: yes sending now, should be in the shared drive.
05:23 Jordan Lee: note — please send sample prompts and a small dataset. we'll do two runs: hosted and dedicated EU to compare p95/p99.
05:31 Mei Chen: about data residency — we have three data classes. class A must stay in EU, class B can be routed, class C public. we'll share definitions.
05:40 Lydia: also need proof of deletion flow for EU PII on request.
05:45 Priya Nair: we have an API for purge + retention controls; i will attach spec.
05:52 Carlos Ortega: procurement — are there penalties for failing to meet latency SLA or is it credits only?
05:58 Marcus Holt: we typically offer service credits tied to p99 thresholds, and can discuss bespoke SLA for enterprise deals.
06:08 Jordan Lee: ok let's recap the decisions so far: 1) NovoMetrics will target a 12-month amendment with 30% uplift; 2) EU sensitive endpoints will be either Private or dedicated EU pool with no-fallback; 3) Redwood to provide pricing and a burst policy worksheet by 8/18; 4) schedule benchmark for 8/24; 5) legal review by Carlos with redlines by 8/25.
06:35 Alex Rui: that's correct, and we'll confirm by 8/20 on EU-only endpoint list.
06:40 Jordan Lee: any final questions?
06:43 Mei Chen: one more — are there recommended quantization profiles for embeddings vs chat? we want to preserve semantic quality for embeddings.
06:50 Priya Nair: for embeddings keep int8 or fp16; for chat you can move to int4 for batch jobs but prefer int8 for interactive. we'll include recommended profiles in the sizing spreadsheet.
06:58 Carlos Ortega: procurement will need the SDSA and SOC docs + sample amendment.
07:04 Marcus Holt: i'll drop links in the follow-up email.
07:08 Jordan Lee: perfect — thanks everyone. we'll send the pricing + docs and lock in the benchmark slot.
07:12 Alex Rui: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
